lines.text: Why does every single car on both sides of the road have to come to a complete stop for a school bus?
In the United States, passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights carries felony-level fines.
American school buses feature a dual amber and red lighting system invented in the late nineteen-fifties.
Amber lights flash to warn motorists that the bus is slowing down to drop off children.
When the bus stops, the driver deploys a mechanical Stop-sign arm and flashes bright red lights.
This creates an enforced pedestrian safety zone around the vehicle because children often run across blind traffic.
School buses are legally the safest form of passenger transportation in the entire country.
